Dear Partners,

We write this quarter from a market that has decided, rather abruptly, to reprice risk all at once. Public equities have slid into bear territory, high-yield spreads have gapped out to 780bps, and the policy rate sits at 5.25% against inflation still running at 4.1%. It is the kind of weather that makes everyone check the barn roof twice. We have checked ours. It is holding.

Stonebeck's reported return for the quarter was -8.5%, bringing the year-to-date figure to -12.0%. Since inception, we remain at +10.0%, and we think that longer arc matters more than any single squall. Our NAV index now stands at 88.0, a mark that reflects real, if uneven, price discovery across the book rather than a wholesale repricing to the tape.

We know the instinct, seeing public equities down -18.0% this quarter against our -8.5%, is to ask whether we are marking generously. We understand the question; we would ask it too if we sat where you sit. Our answer, as it has been, rests on structural seniority: our positions sit ahead of equity and much of the capital structure in every deal we hold, and that seniority is not a marketing phrase, it is the mechanical reason a lender's losses lag an equity holder's losses in a downturn like this one. We are not the same asset as the S&P, and a quarter like this one is precisely why that distinction was built into the strategy from the start.

The constructive amendments we discussed with several of you last quarter — the first covenant conversations this book has ever needed at its current scale — have continued in that same spirit.
